razorhill_kolkar_approach.accept_text: Kolkar Crag is west of Razor Hill, up against the mountains. Kill the centaur you find there, and I don't care which kind. Every wagon that gets through is one I don't have to explain to my cousin Gazlowe in Ratchet, and he isn't a patient goblin.
razorhill_kolkar_approach.turn_in_text:
The drivers say the road under the Crag was quiet this morning, for the first time in a month.

The centaur have a warlord up there giving the orders, and I'll pay more for him if you want the work.

razorhill_rocktusk_farm.description:
Rocktusk Farm sits south of Razor Hill. It was farmland before the Razormane quilboar dug in and made it theirs. Grokk doesn't dress it up: it's contested ground, and right now it's losing to raiders who've got bold enough to hit supply wagons on the open road.

He wants their numbers thinned, the battleguards, the scouts and the geomancers who keep patching the others up mid-fight. Kill enough of them and the farm quiets down for a season, maybe two.
razorhill_rocktusk_farm.accept_text: Battleguard, scout or geomancer, it doesn't matter which order you meet them in, because they're all the same problem in different gear. Kill the geomancer first if you can reach it, or it'll keep healing the others out of spite.
razorhill_rocktusk_farm.turn_in_text: The farm won't stay quiet forever, because it never does, but that buys the road some breathing room, and the wagons stop getting hit for a while. That's good work.

razorhill_scuttle_coast.accept_text: Kill them all, and I won't split hairs over which. The Murloc Tidehunters are vermin, beneath my notice except for how many of my shipments they've ruined, and the deckhands are worse, drowned sailors who forgot they were meant to stay drowned. Neither deserves a separate contract. Thin them out and the road stays open.
razorhill_scuttle_coast.turn_in_text:
The shallows are passable again, which is worth more to me than you probably realise. Every day that coast stays blocked, my margins suffer for it.

You have my gratitude, such as it is, and more usefully, my gold.

razorhill_stormhide_patriarch.description:
The Stormhide Patriarch has ruled Thunder Ridge longer than anyone in Razor Hill can remember. Grokk's own trainer sent a hunting party after it once, when Grokk was young enough to go himself. Three came back. He doesn't say what happened to the rest, and you get the sense he'd rather not be asked.

It roams the ridge instead of keeping a den, so there's no cave to corner it in. There's only open ground, its size, and whatever nerve you can hold onto when something that big charges.
razorhill_stormhide_patriarch.accept_text: It isn't clever, and it doesn't need to be. It's old and it's huge, and it hits like the ridge has decided to fall on you. Don't get greedy with your own hits. Patience beats size in the end. I believe that, because I need to.
razorhill_stormhide_patriarch.turn_in_text:
You actually did it. I'll be honest, I wasn't sure I'd be having this conversation, because that thing outlasted better fighters than either of us.

Thunder Ridge is just a ridge now. Take what it was carrying. You earned every piece of it.

razorhill_supply_run.description: Kravel Coinsnatch is still tallying what he lost before the Kolkar were dealt with. There's cargo scattered along the old caravan route that never got recovered, crates and bolts of cloth worth real money to whoever collects them before they rot or the scavengers pick them over.
razorhill_supply_run.accept_text: Bring back any crates you find along the western route. I'm not proud of how long I've let this sit, but I've been busy, and money left on the ground is still money. I'd rather it was mine.

razorhill_thunder_ridge_approach.description:
Thunder Ridge rises north-east of Razor Hill, a plateau where the thunder lizards nest and the air crackles before a storm that never quite arrives. Grokk has sent recruits up there before. The ones who come back talk about how slow the lizards are, right up until a tail lands on something.

Thin the herd. It's good practice for a fight where speed won't save you and only where you stand will.
razorhill_thunder_ridge_approach.accept_text: They're slow, and that's the trap. Everyone who's died up there got comfortable with slow and forgot what happens when the hit lands. Watch the windup, not the lizard.
razorhill_thunder_ridge_approach.turn_in_text:
You're back, and you're walking without a limp. That's more than I can say for half the recruits I've sent up there.

There's something bigger on that ridge, if you're not done yet: a patriarch, old and mean, that's outlived every hunting party that's gone after it so far.

razorhill_troll_refuge.description: Tal'rashi reached Razor Hill before the Darkspear camp on the Echo Isles had properly taken shape, and he's carried the guilt of it ever since. His kin are still lost to Zalazane's hex, and he found safe ground on the mainland. He can't go back himself, because an injury from the crossing never healed right, but he can ask someone capable to check on his people for him.
razorhill_troll_refuge.accept_text: Find Elder Kang'ari at da camp on da Echo Isles. Tell him Tal'rashi still thinks about dem every day. Dat's all I can send in my place, words, and I hope dey're worth somethin' when dey arrive.

razorhill_warlord_krellian.description: Warlord Krellian holds Kolkar Crag together by reputation, and Kravel has done the sums carefully. Kill the warlord, and either the centaur break into raiding bands too disorganised to hit a moving wagon, or a new warlord takes over in a week. Kravel thinks the odds favour the first, and he's willing to bet a lot of gold on it.
razorhill_warlord_krellian.accept_text: Krellian is what a decade of robbing caravans buys a centaur: confidence, mostly, and the gear to back it up. Kill him fast if you can. Every moment you spend fighting fair gives his lieutenants time to regroup.
razorhill_warlord_krellian.turn_in_text:
That's done, and it's beautiful. I've already got three caravans queued for the western route that were sitting idle waiting for exactly this news.

Do you want to know how profit works? You pay the right person once for a problem that would cost you ten times as much if you left it. Here, you've earned every coin of this.

razorhill_welcome.description:
Weapons Trainer Grokk has watched a hundred valley recruits walk up this road, dusty and a little too pleased with themselves over five dead boars. He doesn't hold it against you. Everyone starts somewhere, and the valley is as gentle as it needs to be.

Razor Hill isn't the valley. Real orcs live here, real quilboar raid the farms south of town, real centaur ride the crags to the west, and something washed-up and wrong still holds the old ruins at Tiragarde Keep on the coast. Grokk wants you to understand the place before he sends you off to bleed in it.
razorhill_welcome.accept_text: Nakhtar's recruits always have that look, as if the valley was the whole world until an hour ago. It wasn't, so ask me what you want to know. Durotar, this town, Orgrimmar, whatever you're standing in the middle of and don't understand yet, I've got time for a few questions. Then I'll let you get on with it.
razorhill_welcome.turn_in_text:
Now you know where you're standing, instead of just knowing you're not in the valley any more. That's worth more than it sounds.

Go and pick a fight with Durotar. It's been waiting.
